title: Finite-free complex fibre homology dimension is upper semicontinuous with quasi-compact sublevel sets
statement: Let $A$ be a ring and let $K$ be a bounded complex [def-pc-derived-category] of finite free $A$-modules, and fix an integer $i$. For each prime $\mathfrak p$ of $A$ put $b_i(\mathfrak p)=\dim_{\kappa(\mathfrak p)}H^i(K\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. Then $b_i$ is upper semicontinuous on $\operatorname{Spec}(A)$, and more precisely: for every integer $r$, the set $\{\mathfrak p:b_i(\mathfrak p)<r\}$ is a finite union of principal opens $D(f)$, $f\in A$; in particular it is open and quasi-compact.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma jump-loci, Tag 0BDI

proof.text: Because $K$ is bounded and each term is finite free, choose bases of $K^{i-1},K^i,K^{i+1}$; the differentials $d^{i-1}$ and $d^i$ are represented by finite matrices $M_{i-1},M_i$ over $A$, and $K\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ in these degrees is the complex of finite-dimensional $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-vector spaces with matrices $M_{i-1}(\mathfrak p),M_i(\mathfrak p)$ (entries reduced at $\mathfrak p$). Put $c=\operatorname{rank}K^i$ and $r_j(\mathfrak p)=\operatorname{rank}M_j(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-matrix-rank]. By [lem-weil-pbc-idempotent-charpoly-rank-nullity] applied to $d^i\otimes\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $\dim\ker=c-r_i(\mathfrak p)$; the image of $d^{i-1}\otimes\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a subspace of this kernel of dimension $r_{i-1}(\mathfrak p)$, and applying the same rank-nullity statement to the quotient map from the kernel onto $H^i$ gives $b_i(\mathfrak p)=c-r_i(\mathfrak p)-r_{i-1}(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma jump-loci, Tag 0BDI

proof.text: Fix a matrix $M$ over $A$ and an integer $s\ge0$. By [def-weil-matrix-rank], $\operatorname{rank}M(\mathfrak p)$ is the largest $k$ with a nonzero $k\times k$ minor of $M(\mathfrak p)$; since a nonzero $k\times k$ minor with $k\ge s$ has, by Laplace expansion, a nonzero $s\times s$ sub-minor, $\operatorname{rank}M(\mathfrak p)\ge s$ iff some $s\times s$ minor of $M(\mathfrak p)$ is nonzero (the $0\times0$ minor is $1$). The determinant commutes with the ring map $A\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, so an $s\times s$ minor $\Delta$ of $M$ reduces to a nonzero element iff $\Delta\notin\mathfrak p$, i.e. $\mathfrak p\in D(\Delta)$. Hence $\{\mathfrak p:\operatorname{rank}M(\mathfrak p)\ge s\}$ is the finite union of $D(\Delta)$ over the $s\times s$ minors $\Delta$ of $M$ (empty if there are none). Intersections of two such finite unions are finite unions of principal opens since $D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg)$.

source.place: Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma jump-loci, Tag 0BDI

proof.text: By Step 1, $b_i(\mathfrak p)<r$ iff $r_i(\mathfrak p)+r_{i-1}(\mathfrak p)>c-r$. Each $r_j(\mathfrak p)$ lies in $\{0,\dots,N_j\}$ with $N_j$ the smaller dimension of $M_j$, so $\{\mathfrak p:b_i(\mathfrak p)<r\}$ is the finite union over pairs $(a,b)$ with $0\le a\le N_i$, $0\le b\le N_{i-1}$, $a+b>c-r$ of $\{r_i\ge a\}\cap\{r_{i-1}\ge b\}$ (take $(a,b)=(r_i(\mathfrak p),r_{i-1}(\mathfrak p))$ for one inclusion). By Step 2 each term, hence the union, is a finite union of principal opens $D(f)$; such a set is open, and quasi-compact because each $D(f)$ is. Thus $b_i$ is upper semicontinuous.
